pinnedSpecials.headline: Record pledges, shrinking NGOs: who gets Bangladesh's aid money
pinnedSpecials.summary: Foreign grants to NGOs are at a seven-year high, yet about 2,200 small NGOs face cuts. Our analysis of six years of data shows the money is reaching fewer, larger organisations.

spotlight.label: Spotlight
spotlight.title: COP31 in Antalya
spotlight.intro: Bangladesh wants adaptation finance tripled and paid as grants, not loans, plus real money for loss and damage. Devlens follows what the summit means for the sector until the talks close.

today.text: The Antalya Leaders' Summit opened with UN Secretary-General António Guterres warning that the climate crisis is "outrunning us" and President Erdoğan pushing a zero-waste pledge. The United States is absent for a second year. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and toured the Bangladesh Pavilion; a meeting with Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng was scheduled, with no read-out yet. He gives Bangladesh's national statement on 12 November. Finance and trade follow on 13 November.

watch: Finance on the agenda: developing countries, led by African states, want tripling adaptation finance formally discussed; developed countries are resisting, and an EU official has warned of no political will for new pledges.
Adaptation finance: whether the COP30 pledge to at least triple it by 2035 gets a baseline, an amount and a delivery plan.
Adaptation indicators: how countries put the 59 Global Goal on Adaptation indicators into practice.
Just transition: whether a mechanism is set up in Antalya, and what it covers.
